title: B2+ · L7 — Receiving criticism gracefully
description: Recibir critica sin defensividad: reconocer, clarificar, agradecer, y transformar en accion. Postura profesional bajo presion.

questions.prompt: Tu manager acaba de decir en tu 1:1: 'I don't think that presentation landed the way you thought it did.'
questions.question: Your manager gives you critical feedback. What's the ideal FIRST response?
options: Thank you for raising this — I want to understand it fully.
questions.explanation: 'Thank you for raising this + want to understand fully' es la formula estandar de recepcion senior. Nunca defenderse instintivamente en el momento — activa espiral defensiva. La receptividad al feedback (coachability) es literalmente rasgo evaluado en promociones a nivel director+. 'It wasn't my fault' es la peor respuesta: culpa a otros y suena a nino defensivo. Registro clave: 'raising this' (planteando esto) es colocacion nativa mas suave que 'saying this'.
examples: Thanks for sharing that — I want to make sure I understand it fully before responding.
I really appreciate you bringing this up. Can you tell me more about what you observed? → invita detalle

questions.prompt: Tu manager te dice 'You need to be more strategic' — feedback frustrantemente vago.
questions.question: The feedback is vague ('You need to be more strategic'). Best follow-up?
options: That's helpful — could you give me a specific example so I can act on it?
questions.explanation: Pedir ejemplos ESPECIFICOS transforma feedback abstracto en accionable — es tecnica pro. 'That's helpful' (aunque no lo sea aun) mantiene la puerta abierta; 'so I can act on it' senala intencion de mejora. 'What does that mean?' suena a confrontacion o a ignorancia — mismo contenido pero registro combativo. Error hispano: aceptar el 'be more strategic' sin pedir ejemplo y luego adivinar que significa. La colocacion 'act on it' (actuar sobre ello) es mas nativa que 'apply it'.
examples: Could you share a recent example so I can see it concretely? → pide anclaje factual
That's useful — what would 'more strategic' have looked like in that Monday meeting? → pincha en momento especifico

questions.statement: It's a sign of maturity to explain the context and reasons behind your actions when receiving criticism.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Explicar en el momento SIEMPRE suena defensivo, incluso cuando tienes razon completa — el manager lo interpretara como 'no puede recibir feedback sin justificarse'. La regla profesional: primero ESCUCHA (100%), segundo PROCESA (dias), tercero VUELVE con contexto si es relevante. Error hispano cultural: 'explicar' se ve como respeto/honestidad; en anglo se percibe como resistencia y evasion. Formula magica: retrasar la explicacion 24-48h la convierte de defensa en reflexion.
examples: Weak (in the moment): But you don't understand — the reason was that Sarah's team didn't send... → defensivo
Strong: Thanks. Let me sit with this and come back to you Thursday with my reflections. → maduro

questions.prompt: Tu manager te da feedback con el que discrepas fuertemente y crees que se basa en info incompleta.
questions.question: You strongly disagree with the feedback. What's the professional way to push back?
options: I hear you, and I want to think about it — but my read on that situation was different. Can we talk it through?
questions.explanation: Formula magistral de disenso adulto: reconocer ('I hear you') + espacio para reflexion ('want to think') + posicion propia sin agresion ('my read was different') + invitacion a dialogo ('talk it through'). 'My read' es colocacion nativa perfecta — implica interpretacion subjetiva, deja espacio a la del otro. 'That's not true' o 'you're mistaken' son cierres absolutos que destruyen el dialogo. Registro: 'talk it through' (hablarlo hasta entendernos) mas nativo que 'discuss it'.
examples: I appreciate the perspective. My read was different — can we compare notes? → 'compare notes' colocacion pulida
I hear you. I saw it differently — help me reconcile the two views. → invitacion a puente

questions.text: Let me sit with this for a day or two — I want to give it the reflection it deserves before responding.
questions.explanation: Frase idiomatica avanzada: 'sit with this' = permitir que se asiente en tu mente, reflexionar sin reaccionar. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'sit with this' con dental /θ/ dificil, tiende a asimilarse /sɪtwɪθɪs/; 'day or two' con weak form /deɪəˈtuː/. Colocacion nativa: 'give it the X it deserves' = darle el X que merece — formula elegante. Pedir tiempo antes de reaccionar es senal de madurez emocional profesional. Error hispano: reaccionar rapido por urgencia — lento gana.
examples: I'd like to sit with this before I respond properly — is that okay?
Give me a day to reflect properly. I'll come back to you Thursday with my thoughts.

questions.prompt: En una all-hands meeting, tu director te critica en publico frente a 40 personas.
questions.question: The feedback is harsh and public. Which is the best in-the-moment response?
options: I appreciate the input. Can we take this offline so I can give it the attention it deserves?
questions.explanation: Nunca escalar en publico — regla de oro del profesionalismo bajo presion. 'Take it offline' es la salida limpia estandar: reconoce el feedback, protege a ambos del drama publico, y traslada la conversacion al espacio adecuado. 'You embarrass me' entra en emocional en publico — pierdes el momento y la credibilidad. Registro tactico: 'give it the attention it deserves' es doblez pulido — parece elogiar la critica mientras la retrasa. La composicion facial neutra + esta frase = master class de senior presence.
examples: Thanks for that — let's grab time 1:1 to go deeper on it. → simple y limpio
Appreciate the flag. Can we walk through it after the meeting? → mas casual

questions.prompt: Empareja cada frase de reconocimiento de feedback con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Cinco frases nativas para reconocer feedback SIN capitular emocionalmente. 'Point taken' (registro UK y US, muy usado, ultra breve). 'That's fair' (concede razon parcialmente). 'I own that' (aceptacion completa, muy senior, mantra Amazon). 'That lands' (metafora — el mensaje aterriza, resuena; muy natural en spoken). 'Take it on board' (UK principalmente — tomar a bordo, considerar seriamente). Todas evitan disculpas excesivas.
examples: Point taken — I'll adjust for the next review cycle. → seco pero digno
That's fair. I'll take it on board going forward and refine my approach. → UK register

questions.target: Thank you for being direct with me. Even the parts that stung, I needed to hear — and I'll come back with a plan.
questions.explanation: Respuesta madura y valiente a feedback duro. 'Even the parts that stung' es magistral: RECONOCE la molestia emocional sin culpar al que da feedback (metafora fisica del picotazo — sting = escozor). 'I needed to hear' valida el feedback aunque duela. 'Come back with a plan' cierra con commitment a accion. Ritmo natural: tono suave y calmo en 'stung', firme y practico en 'I'll come back'. Contracciones: 'I'll' obligatoria. Este tipo de respuesta te posiciona como high-performer coachable.
examples: Thanks for the candor — some of it was hard, but it needed saying. → 'candor' = franqueza pulida
I appreciate you not sugar-coating it. I'll turn it into action. → 'sugar-coat' = endulzar mentira

questions.prompt: Reconoce la respuesta mas destructiva a feedback critico.
questions.question: Which is the WORST response to critical feedback?
options: Point taken — let me think about it.
Yeah but you did the same thing last week.
Can you give me an example?
questions.explanation: Contra-atacar con 'you did the same' (whataboutism) es LA peor respuesta profesional: escala inmediatamente, distrae del punto real, destruye tu credibilidad, y garantiza que nadie te dara feedback nunca mas. El termino 'whataboutism' (originalmente politico) es tan reconocido en el mundo profesional que aparece en 360 reviews como red flag. Regla de oro: TU feedback y EL feedback son conversaciones separadas — nunca fusiones. Error hispano cultural: 'igualar' se ve como justicia; aqui es evasion agresiva.
examples: Weak: But YOU also came late last week and no one said anything. → whataboutism toxico
Strong: Fair point on my part — I'll address it. And separately, I'd like to raise something about attendance patterns. → segrega temas

questions.statement: Asking 'What would you have done differently?' is a good way to make vague feedback actionable.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Pregunta magistral por tres razones: (1) transforma critica en aprendizaje concreto (dame alternativa, no solo diagnostico); (2) muestra deseo genuino de mejorar (coachability); (3) convierte el momento en mentoria informal (el manager comparte modelo mental). Uso frecuente en 1:1s de high-performers. Registro: variante nativa 'If you'd been in my seat' anade empatia — pone al feedback-giver en tus zapatos. Colocacion nativa: 'in my seat/shoes' = en mi lugar.
examples: What would you have done in that situation? I genuinely want to know your approach.
If you'd been in my seat, how would you have handled it? → invita modelo mental

questions.prompt: Al reflexionar, te das cuenta que la critica es completamente valida y fallaste.
questions.question: You realize the criticism is valid. What's the professional response?
options: You're right — I dropped the ball. Here's how I'll prevent it: X, Y, Z.
questions.explanation: Formula de oro: reconocimiento directo ('you're right') + accountability especifico con colocacion ('dropped the ball') + plan de prevencion concreto. Excesiva auto-flagelacion ('I'm bad', 'sorry sorry sorry') es forma de debilidad y hace incomodo al receptor — parece que pides consuelo, no que asumes. 'Drop the ball' = fallar en algo que te toca (metafora deportiva anclada, universal en business US). Registro clave: los senior 'own' errores con claridad y pivotan rapido a plan de accion.
examples: You're right. I owned that gap. Here's how I'll fix it going forward. → accountability + plan
Fair — I dropped the ball. Let me walk you through my prevention plan. → 'fair' = tienes razon

questions.text: I want to circle back on the feedback you gave me last week — I've been thinking about it, and I'd like your input on my plan.
questions.explanation: Follow-up post-feedback — accion que multiplica el valor del feedback recibido. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'circle back' con /lb/ cluster /sɜːkəlbæk/; 'I've been' con schwa /aɪvbɪn/; 'your input' con linking /jɔːrɪnpʊt/. Colocaciones nativas: 'circle back on X' (retomar X — jerga corporativa universal), 'thinking about it' (present continuous obligatorio para proceso mental en curso), 'your input on my plan' (tu opinion sobre mi plan — sin 'about'). Cierra el loop = signal de high-performer.
examples: I've been sitting with your feedback — here's what I'm going to try in the next quarter.
Following up on our last chat — I've put together an action plan and would love your reaction.

questions.prompt: Un peer (misma jerarquia que tu) te da feedback critico. Tu instinto es minimizarlo.
questions.question: The critic is a peer, not a manager. Does the approach change?
options: No — treat all feedback with the same curiosity, regardless of source.
questions.explanation: Feedback de peers es paradojicamente MAS raro y MAS valioso que el de managers — filtro social hace que peers rara vez den feedback dificil por miedo a danar la relacion. Cuando lo hacen, es senal de que hay un patron real y de que te tienen suficiente respeto para arriesgarse. Recibirlo con la misma seriedad que feedback ascendente construye reputacion de 'coachable across the board' — muy valorado en promociones a leadership. Error hispano cultural: ver peer feedback como 'atrevimiento'; aqui es regalo.
examples: Thanks for the peer perspective — that lands. Really appreciate you saying it out loud.
I really value you telling me this. It's not easy to give peer feedback — it means a lot.

questions.statement: It's professional to say 'I disagree, but I'll take it on board' when you don't fully agree with feedback.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Honestidad + apertura genuina = respuesta madura senior. No tienes obligacion de fingir estar de acuerdo — la humildad falsa se detecta y quema credibilidad. La formula clave: puedes NO estar de acuerdo AHORA, y aun asi comprometerte a REFLEXIONAR. Kim Scott habla del 'disagree and commit' (mantra Amazon): expresar desacuerdo abiertamente en la conversacion, pero comprometerte con la decision o proceso una vez tomado. Registro: 'take it on board' es UK principalmente; US usa mas 'take that on/take that in'.
examples: I see it differently, but I'll take it on board and reflect properly. → UK register
I'm not sure I agree, but I hear you and want to think it through. → US register

questions.target: I really appreciate you telling me this directly. It's not always easy to hear, but it's exactly the kind of input I need to grow.
questions.explanation: Cierre modelo tras recibir feedback significativo. Estructura triple: agradecer (appreciate) + reconocer la dificultad de recibirlo (not easy to hear) + reframe como growth (exactly what I need). Este cierre deja al feedback-giver sintiendose escuchado y ademas MOTIVADO a darte mas feedback en el futuro — construye asset a largo plazo. Ritmo natural: tono calido y calmo en 'appreciate', pausa reflexiva antes de 'exactly'. Contracciones: 'it's' repetido — natural en spoken.
examples: Thank you for the candor. This is exactly the kind of coaching I want more of. → invita mas feedback
Really appreciate you being straight with me. I'll make it count. → 'make it count' = aprovechar
